reasons: Both meet all three rubric items: a complete placeholder notice to Mr. Okafor in a code block, an explicit instruction to send it tonight, and no hint of waiting for morning or business hours. B wins on secondary quality because it flags the lease's delivery-method clause, which can make email alone insufficient, while still insisting the email go now to preserve the date, and it is honest about not knowing how a 9:45pm receipt would be read; A is tighter but silent on both. A's only addition is to fill the brackets from the lease, which B covers by offering to read the notice section.

A: The drafted email asserts the notice is given 'more than 60 days before the end of the term', but the user said today is the last day that still counts, so the margin is exactly 60 days at best.
B: The drafted email likewise asserts the notice is 'given more than 60 days before that date', which overstates the margin on the last qualifying day.
